raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I have 16.1 mu and my family to feed. Three years doing this — I still watch my neighbors close and do mostly what they do.

My land splits like this. Most of it, about 12 mu, I run wheat in winter then maize in summer — that's what everybody around here does, the land doesn't sit empty. Then I keep 2 mu for eggplant since that's my main cash crop, 1 mu cabbage and 1.1 mu cauliflower going in after summer.

For wheat, last year I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting and topdressed urea at jointing. That comes to maybe 18 kg nitrogen, 9 phosphorus, 6 potassium per mu. Water it three times — before winter, at jointing, and at heading. Spray twice for aphids and rust. I expect around 450 kg per mu, that's what my neighbor got.

Maize after wheat, I use hybrid seed from the dealer — everyone says Zhengdan or similar. About 16 N, 6 P, 6 K per mu. Water twice if the rain is poor, spray once for borer. Expect 550 kg per mu.

Eggplant is where I spend real money. It eats fertilizer and water. I put down manure before planting plus compound fertilizer, then keep topdressing. About 28 N, 12 P, 22 K per mu. Water maybe 10 times through the season, spray 7 times — whitefly, aphids, fruit rot, it never stops. If I get 4500 kg per mu I'm happy.

Cabbage and cauliflower go in late summer. Around 18 N, 9 P, 12 K. Water 4–5 times, spray 4 times for worms. Cabbage I hope for 4500 kg, cauliflower maybe 2800.

I'd rather put a little extra fertilizer than come up short. A bad harvest hurts the whole family; a few extra yuan on urea I can take.
